records.name: Organizational Research Methods
records.publisher: Sage; sponsored by the Research Methods Division of the Academy of Management
records.scope_notes: Methodological advances for organizational science: comparisons and improvements of quantitative or qualitative methods, computational procedures, and practical methodological syntheses. Routine substantive applications of an existing method are discouraged; an organizational research contribution is required.

route.conditions: Choose standard subscription publication. Optional open access and specifically requested print color can incur fees. Short methodological reports allow 18 text pages; regular papers are encouraged to remain within 40 pages inclusive.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None stated for standard compliant articles; paid open access and requested print color are optional.

fee_evidence.note: Journal-specific instructions explicitly establish no submission or publication fees. Paid Sage Choice open access is a separate option.

difficulty.basis: Discovery did not establish acceptance selectivity or comparative difficulty.

records.name: Social Science Computer Review
records.scope_notes: Computational social science, digital communities, social media, AI-assisted analysis, social effects of information technologies, and computing methods for social research. route.conditions: Choose standard subscription publication within the stated 10,000-word maximum. route.other_mandatory_costs: None stated for standard compliant articles; paid open access and requested print color are optional.

records.name: Organization Studies

records.scope_notes: General sociology with theoretical, conceptual or empirical contributions advancing existing debates. records.name: Network Science
records.scope_notes: Original work and surveys on mathematical, computational, empirical and substantive network-data collection, analysis, modeling and visualization. Relevant to collaboration networks and computational sociology when the network contribution is central.

route.conditions: Fully gold OA since 2024; no current subscription publication route. The fee page promises an APC waiver after acceptance for authors without an institutional agreement and without funding, with no proof of lack of funding required. Waiver requests are administered by Cambridge after editorial acceptance. This is a conditional no-cost publication route; inspected pages did not explicitly settle submission fees.
route.other_mandatory_costs: No other compulsory cost found in inspected pages; submission charge status remains unconfirmed.

fee_evidence.note: Current gold-OA fee page gives an APC and promises a post-acceptance waiver for authors without institutional coverage or funding; lack of funding does not require proof.
Policy describes post-acceptance waiver requests and separates funding status from editorial acceptance; this is not a diamond or unconditional free route.

difficulty.basis: Discovery did not establish acceptance selectivity or comparative difficulty.

notes: Ten journal candidates: eight journal-specific verified free subscription routes and two conservatively pending fee verification. Optional OA and print-color charges remain separate.

Current official publisher and journal pages were inspected. No citation metrics or acceptance rates were imported; difficulty remains unknown for the ranking role. OSRI relevance is an interpretation of venue scope, not editorial preapproval.

The concentration of verified routes at Sage reflects explicit journal-specific fee wording. Springer and Cambridge candidates retain uncertainty rather than being promoted from no-APC language to guaranteed zero total cost.

Other investigated leads were omitted: official Social Networks homepage and guide returned HTTP 403; Journal of Mathematical Sociology official author instructions also returned HTTP 403. Secondary no-fee listings were not accepted as conclusive official evidence.
Sociological Methods & Research explicitly offers no-fee subscription publication, but inspected instructions did not explicitly settle submission fees; omitted to keep discovery bounded at ten.

Organization Studies changed regular research articles to empirical work from June 2025. Current Sociology has conflicting preprint wording. The Sociological Review explicitly bars posted preprints. Retain these distinctions in manuscript planning.
Agent discovery is not human scientific review, editorial acceptance, or confirmation of manuscript-specific fit.
